bill.plainSummary: This bill directs federal agencies to review and simplify the paperwork and application processes for Medicare, Medicaid, the Children's Health Insurance Program, and Social Security. bill.title: A joint resolution proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States relating to contributions and expenditures intended to affect elections.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: Organizations that spend money to influence elections would face new potential restrictions on their expenditures and fundraising.
The amendment would create new constitutional authority to regulate campaign finance, directly affecting election law practice and lobbying activity.
Limits on campaign spending could affect demand for political advertising across broadcast, digital, and print media platforms.
The amendment's authorization to distinguish between natural persons and corporations could affect how financial institutions participate in election-related spending.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would allow Congress and state governments to set limits on how much money candidates and others can raise and spend to influence elections. It would also permit lawmakers to treat corporations and other legal entities differently from individual people, including by prohibiting those entities from spending money on elections. The amendment would require ratification by three-fourths of the states to take effect.

bill.title: Keeping All Students Safe Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates schools and Head Start programs, imposing new training requirements, compliance procedures, and enforcement obligations on educational institutions.
The bill creates a new private right of action for students subjected to unlawful seclusion or restraint, which would generate litigation opportunities.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit schools and Head Start programs that receive federal funding from using seclusion (confining a student alone in a locked room) and would restrict the use of physical restraints to situations where a student poses an imminent danger of serious physical injury. It requires staff training in crisis intervention, establishes procedures for reporting incidents, and creates enforcement mechanisms including the ability for students to sue and for federal agencies to withhold payments from programs that violate the rules. The bill also provides grants to help state education agencies implement these policies.

plain.whoItTouches: Students, teachers, and the families paying for it.

bill.title: Combating Organized Retail Crime Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The bill directly addresses organized theft targeting retail operations and e-commerce platforms.
The bill explicitly covers theft from interstate and foreign shipments, affecting logistics and shipping companies.
The bill addresses online marketplaces and social media platforms where stolen goods are sold, potentially creating new compliance obligations.
The bill expands money laundering statutes to cover prepaid cards and gift cards, affecting payment processors and card issuers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill expands federal authority to prosecute organized retail theft and supply-chain crime. It allows prosecutors to aggregate the value of stolen goods over a 12-month period to meet felony thresholds, makes these offenses predicate crimes for money laundering charges, and authorizes asset forfeiture. The bill also creates a temporary coordination center within the Department of Homeland Security to help federal agencies work together on these cases.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who uses the internet.

bill.title: Emergency Conservation Program Improvement Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-102.

industries.rationale: The bill directly expands cost-sharing payments and advance funding for agricultural producers repairing farmland and conservation structures after disasters.
Expanded federal disaster assistance may affect demand for private agricultural and forestry insurance products.

bill.plainSummary: This bill expands two federal programs that help farmers and forest landowners recover from natural disasters. It increases the percentage of costs that can be paid upfront before work begins, extends the time recipients have to use the funds from 60 to 180 days, and makes landowners eligible for assistance when damage from human-caused wildfires spreads due to natural conditions or when federal actions cause the fire. The changes apply to the Emergency Conservation Program and the Emergency Forest Restoration Program.

plain.whoItTouches: Farmers, and anyone who buys food.

bill.title: New Mexico Land Grant-Mercedes Historical or Traditional Use Cooperation and Coordination Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 476.

industries.rationale: The bill addresses authorization processes for livestock grazing and other traditional agricultural uses on federal lands by land grant communities.
The bill affects land use and access rights on federal lands that were historically part of community land grants, potentially influencing property use patterns.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the Bureau of Land Management and the Forest Service to create a formal agreement with the New Mexico Land Grant Council. The agreement would outline how the 27 recognized community land grants—descendants of Spanish and Mexican land grants whose lands became federal property—can obtain permission for traditional uses like grazing livestock, maintaining cemeteries, or using roads and water on what is now federal land. Federal agencies would also be required to assess how their land-use plans affect these historical community practices.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who drives. People who live near or work on federal land.

bill.title: A joint resolution to direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Venezuela that have not been authorized by Congress.
bill.latestActionText: Point of order that the measure is not entitled to expedited procedures under 50 U.S.C. 1546(a) raised against the measure agreed to in Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 50 - 50. Record Vote Number: 9.

industries.rationale: The resolution would directly affect the deployment and operational scope of U.S. Armed Forces and defense contractors supporting military operations in the Venezuela region.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would require the President to end any U.S. military operations in or against Venezuela unless Congress has formally declared war or authorized the use of force. It preserves the President's authority to defend the United States from an armed attack or imminent threat. The measure addresses congressional oversight of military deployments and the constitutional division of war powers.

plain.whoItTouches: Mostly people outside the United States. It reaches most readers here only indirectly.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
